title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #152 review (frontend-support-resistance-overlay)
description: Tracked non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #152 (frontend-support-resistance-overlay), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. Distinct from the PR's own blocking findings (the zone-band price-scale autoscale distortion, and the single-visible-bar setData crash risk), which stay on frontend-support-resistance-overlay itself and must be fixed before that PR can be accepted.

checklist.step: supportResistanceZoneHelp/falseBreakoutHelp's interpretValue functions (metricHelpContent.ts) read from the full (up to 15) zones array passed in from PriceChart.tsx, not the MAX_DISPLAYED_ZONES=6-capped, currently-visible-date-range-windowed subset the chart actually draws (buildZoneRenderData/buildFalseBreakoutMarkers apply that capping/windowing, but the two MetricHelp call sites pass the unfiltered `zones` array straight through). The legend balloon can therefore describe a 'nearest zone' or 'most recent false breakout' that has no corresponding shaded band/marker/price-line anywhere on the visible chart, which is confusing on its own. Fix direction: pass the same capped/windowed subset (or at least filter by the same MAX_DISPLAYED_ZONES slice, and for falseBreakoutHelp also the current visible date range) into interpretValue that the chart-drawing effects use. NOTE: PR #152's retry-round-1 fix (commit 4f1a1f4) added a price-relevance filter (selectDisplayedZones) on top of this same gap, which escalated this from 'confusing' to actively misleading (see review.comments on the parent task's retry-round-1 review) and was recorded as BLOCKING on that PR -- if it's already been fixed by the time this follow-up is picked up, close this item out as resolved rather than duplicating the work.

The 50%-price-ratio relevance window (isZoneRelevant/ZONE_RELEVANCE_PRICE_RATIO, PriceChart.tsx, added in PR #152 retry-round-1 commit 4f1a1f4) is anchored only to the latest visible close, not to the currently-visible bars' own price span. pr-reviewer's retry-round-1 re-review stress-tested this with a synthetic zone ~40% above the latest close (inside the 50% window, so treated as relevant) against a 1-month preset range: the y-axis stretched to squash the actual candlestick/EMA/channel content into roughly the same fraction of the pane (~11%) as the original reported autoscale-distortion bug -- the same zone against a 1-year view was fine (more natural price spread to absorb it). Real zones are strength-scored independent of price distance, so a strong zone 30-45% from today's price is plausible for some ticker/time even though none of AAPL/NVDA/MSFT/AMD's currently-cached data hit this band during that review. Not blocking (bounded distortion, ~2.25x worst case, and a real tradeoff already reasoned through in that PR's decisions entry) but worth reconsidering: an approach that also accounts for the actually-visible bars' own high/low range (e.g. intersecting the ratio window with a multiple of the visible span), not a fixed ratio off the latest close alone.
